t:
Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Attorney General shall provide direction and guidance for the following:
    (1) Training programs.—Programs that offer specialized and comprehensive training, in procedures to identify and appropriately respond to incidents in which the unique needs of individuals who have a mental illness are involved, to first responders and tactical units of—
        (A) Federal law enforcement agencies; and 
        (B) other Federal criminal justice agencies such as the Bureau of Prisons, the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, and other agencies that the Attorney General determines appropriate.  
    (2) Improved technology.—The establishment of, or improvement of existing, computerized information systems to provide timely information to employees of Federal law enforcement agencies, and Federal criminal justice agencies to improve the response of such employees to situations involving individuals who have a mental illness.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "direction and guidance" amounts to rulemaking, or that training for first responders brings in outside parties. But the guidance is aimed only at Federal law enforcement and Federal criminal justice agencies and their employees, and the section requires no public comment, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with states, experts, or the public. Every actor is inside the federal government, so this is not participation.
fable.s: the Attorney General shall provide direction and guidance for the following

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Attorney General to provide direction and guidance for training programs and technology improvements for federal employees. All actors involved (the Attorney General, federal law enforcement agencies, and other federal criminal justice agencies) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations before making these decisions.
qwen_block.s: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Attorney General shall provide direction and guidance for the following: (1) Training programs.—Programs that offer specialized and comprehensive training... to first responders and tactical units of (A) Federal law enforcement agencies; and (B) other Federal criminal justice agencies...

opus.w: The Attorney General must give direction and guidance on training programs and information systems for federal law enforcement and federal criminal justice agencies only. No states, experts, the public or other outside parties are consulted, and the section requires no regulation, comment period or hearing. Reading "guidance" as rulemaking would stretch the text, and in any case everyone involved is inside the federal government.
opus.s: the Attorney General shall provide direction and guidance for the following:
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** "provide direction and guidance" might look like rulemaking or a formal policy process, which would count as participation. That reading fails. The section never requires regulations, a comment period, or a hearing, and every party it names is federal: the Attorney General, Federal law enforcement agencies, the Bureau of Prisons and the Administrative Office of the United States Courts. No one outside the federal government takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Attorney General to provide direction for training programs and technology improvements for federal law enforcement and criminal justice agencies. All actors mentioned (Federal law enforcement agencies, Bureau of Prisons, etc.) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with people outside the government, such as the general public, states, or non-profits.
qwen_chat.s: Training programs.—Programs that offer specialized and comprehensive training, in procedures to identify and appropriately respond to incidents in which the unique needs of individuals who have a mental illness are involved, to first responders and tactical units of— (A) Federal law enforcement agencies; and (B) other Federal criminal justice agencies such as the Bureau of Prisons, the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, and other agencies that the Attorney General determines appropriate.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that providing training to "first responders" or improving technology for "employees" constitutes participation because it involves interaction with people. However, the definition explicitly states that if every actor involved is inside the federal government (federal agencies, federal employees), the answer is "No". The section only mandates internal training and system improvements for federal employees; it does not require consultation with the public, states, or other outside entities.
